subject.title: fix: resolve Codex fork duplication when parent is unresolved (#2108)

question: Should CodexBar adopt this turn-ID parent-scoped row ownership model, consolidate it with the parent-fingerprint and leaf-identity design in https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2118, or retain the merged fail-open policy until a fuller family ledger is implemented?
rationale: The merged design intentionally avoids destructive missing-parent deduplication, while two open PRs propose different partial provenance and cache contracts; code review alone cannot choose the permanent accounting contract safely.

options.title: Consolidate the designs
options.body: Use one branch to combine reliable leaf identity, parent dependency invalidation, turn provenance, cross-window ownership migration, and affected-corpus proof.

options.title: Narrow this PR
options.body: Limit this PR to mechanics that do not change ambiguous missing-parent ownership and leave full sibling deduplication to the canonical ledger work.

options.title: Keep fail-open
options.body: Do not merge either destructive deduplication path until a complete family ledger and collision policy are proven on the affected corpus.

recommendation.title: Consolidate the designs
recommendation.body: Use one branch to combine reliable leaf identity, parent dependency invalidation, turn provenance, cross-window ownership migration, and affected-corpus proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the existing intentional fail-open design and is best positioned to choose the repository's permanent accounting contract.
